extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting to Nature Portfolio journals, researchers, institutional press offices, and journalists covering Nature Portfolio content
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and guidance governing how authors, researchers, institutional press offices, and journalists should communicate about submissions, accepted papers, preprints, conference presentations, and press releases for Nature Portfolio journals, including embargo rules, press-release distribution, and sanctions for breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discouragement of direct solicitation of media for submitted material
rubrics_metrics.description: We strongly discourage authors and potential authors from direct solicitation of media coverage of material they have submitted to Nature and the Nature Portfolio journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted contributions can be discussed with the media only once the publication date has been confirmed and no more than a week before the publication date under our embargo conditions. See the 'Communication between scientists' section for how embargo applies to preprints and conference presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and conditions for authors to discuss accepted contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted contributions may be discussed with the media only once the publication date has been confirmed and no more than a week before the publication date under our embargo conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not promote or solicit media coverage of submitted material before acceptance; discussion is limited to the confirmed publication window and remains subject to the stated embargo time and date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature press-release distribution procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature produces and distributes press releases summarizing upcoming content to a list of registered journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists are encouraged to read the full paper and are given names and contact details of corresponding authors. They receive access to the full text of papers about a week before publication on a password-protected website, together with related material (e.g., News and Views, extra images).

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo on press releases and associated content
rubrics_metrics.description: The content of the press release and papers is embargoed until the time and date clearly stated on the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists and authors must respect the stated embargo; early disclosure undermines the intent of fair access and informed reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlighting especially newsworthy papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers that are deemed especially newsworthy are highlighted by a brief summary on the press release for that journal, written by the editors and the press office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such highlighting may prompt media contact with authors; authors are encouraged to cooperate with journalists to ensure accurate and balanced coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors' own publicity must adhere to embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors whose papers are scheduled for publication may arrange their own publicity (for instance through their institutional press offices), but they must strictly adhere to our media embargo and are advised to coordinate their own publicity with our press office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination helps ensure consistency between journal and institutional messaging and prevents premature release of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for embargo policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargo policy aims to provide fair and equal access to media, allowing informed comment based on the complete and final version of the paper to be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy serves scientists, authors, journalists and the public by enabling informed reactions based on peer-reviewed content. Premature release denies journalists confidence and removes their ability to obtain independent reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction for journalists breaking embargoes
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists who break our embargoes have been removed from the press-release circulation list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal from the circulation list is an enforcement mechanism; the journal will continue to use this sanction when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for open communication between researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Portfolio journals support open communications between researchers, including posting on recognised community preprint servers, preprint commenting platforms, discussions at research meetings, and on authors' blogs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neither conference presentations nor posting on recognized preprint servers constitute prior publication for the purposes of submission to Nature journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on media responses about preprints and conference presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers may respond to requests from the media in response to a preprint or conference presentation by providing explanation or clarification of the work, or information about its context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such media coverage will not hinder editorial handling of a submission, but may reduce or pre-empt coverage at time of publication. Researchers approached by reporters should make clear the paper has not yet undergone peer review, that findings are provisional, and that conclusions may change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality expectation about peer review and editorial process
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are expected to keep the details of the peer review and editorial process confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disclose peer-review correspondence or editorial deliberations; maintain confidentiality even when discussing preprints or interacting with journalists about submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation for reporters covering preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: We recommend that reporters who cover preprints clearly indicate that the study has not been peer reviewed and that the claims may change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should explicitly state the provisional status of preprint findings to avoid misleading readers about the level of validation the work has received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission to display drafts on established preprint servers
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientists may display drafts of their research papers on an established preprint server before or during submission to Nature or any Nature journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exposure of preprints on servers does not preempt submission; posting preprints is supported but should be accompanied by statements about review status when engaging with media.
